entries.title: A day with western lowland gorillas
entries.answer: Western lowland gorillas live in forests in central Africa. They walk on the ground a great deal, often resting their weight on their knuckles. They also climb and reach for food in trees. A gorilla group spends part of the day moving among places where it can eat fruit, leaves, and stems. A mature male often leads the group. He can be recognized by the lighter hair that grows across his back, giving rise to the name silverback.
facts: Gorillas are great apes.
Some gorillas eat insects as well as plants.

entries.title: A ferret that depends on prairie dogs
entries.answer: A black-footed ferret may spend much of the day underground in tunnels dug by prairie dogs. It also hunts prairie dogs for food, following them through narrow passages where larger animals could not fit. When wide areas of prairie were lost and many prairie dog colonies disappeared, black-footed ferrets became very rare. A small group found in Wyoming helped people raise ferrets for release. Recovery requires land with enough prairie dogs to feed wild ferrets and provide burrows.
facts: Black-footed ferrets usually hunt at night.
The black-footed ferret is the only ferret native to North America.

entries.title: A giant lizard from Indonesian islands
entries.answer: The Komodo dragon is a real animal found on a few islands in Indonesia. It is the largest kind of lizard alive today. A Komodo dragon flicks its tongue out and picks up tiny traces from the air. Inside its mouth, an organ helps it read those traces and find food. Young dragons often spend time in trees, where they are safer from larger Komodo dragons. Heavy adults spend most of their time on the ground.
facts: Large Komodo dragons can be about ten feet long.
Komodo dragons have forked tongues.

entries.title: A red panda’s life in the trees
entries.answer: Look carefully at a branch in an Asian mountain forest and a red panda might be resting around it. This small mammal has reddish fur and a ringed tail. It can use its bushy tail to help balance and curl it around its body in cold weather. Much of its food is bamboo, even though it belongs to a different animal family from the giant panda. Red pandas grip branches as they climb with curved claws.
facts: Red pandas can climb down a tree headfirst.
Red pandas have a thumb-like wrist bone that helps them grasp bamboo.

entries.title: Bats and how they find their way
entries.answer: Bats are mammals and can fly by flapping their wings. Their wings are made of thin skin stretched over long fingers. Many kinds of bats fly in the dark and use sound to find their way. A bat makes a call and listens for the sound to bounce back. The echo may tell the bat where a moth or a branch is. This is called echolocation. Bats can also see. Many eat insects, but some kinds eat fruit or drink nectar from flowers.
facts: Bats are the only mammals that can fly by flapping their wings.
Some bats can carry pollen between flowers.

entries.title: Can a porcupine throw its quills?
entries.answer: A North American porcupine does not toss its quills across the air. The quills are stiff hairs that come loose if an animal bumps into them. Tiny hooks near their tips can hold them in place after they stick. Before that happens, the porcupine can raise its quills and turn its back toward danger. It often climbs trees to eat leaves, buds, or bark. When it is feeding quietly, the quills may lie fairly flat.
facts: Porcupines grow new quills if old ones come loose.
A North American porcupine is a rodent.

entries.title: How a beaver makes a pond
entries.answer: A beaver can turn a shallow stream into a pond by piling branches and mud across it. Water slows down behind the dam and spreads into a wider area. That water helps a beaver move branches and swim safely to its home. A home built from sticks and mud is called a lodge. It can have an opening under the pond’s surface. Other animals can find food and shelter in the wet ground and open water created by a beaver dam.
facts: Beavers gnaw through branches with strong front teeth.
A lodge is a beaver’s home. A dam holds water back.

entries.title: How an alligator lives on land and in water
entries.answer: An American alligator can float with much of its body hidden below the surface. Its eyes and nostrils sit high enough to stay above the water while it waits. A strong tail helps it swim in marshes, ponds, and rivers. Alligators can dig deep places that hold water when a wetland dries out. Fish and other animals may gather in those holes during dry times, so an alligator can help shape the wetland it lives in.
facts: American alligators live in the southeastern United States.
A mother alligator guards her nest and can protect her young.

entries.title: How does a giant anteater eat without teeth?
entries.answer: A giant anteater has a long, narrow face and no teeth. When it finds an ant or termite nest, it can rake open a small spot with its front claws. It reaches inside with a long tongue coated with sticky spit. Insects cling to the tongue and are pulled into the mouth as the tongue flicks back and forth. An anteater moves among nests rather than emptying one nest at a time.
facts: A giant anteater’s tongue can reach roughly two feet.
Its front claws are long, so it bends them out of the way when it walks.

entries.title: How does a sea lion walk on a beach?
entries.answer: A California sea lion can turn its back flippers forward and use them to walk on land. That makes it easier to move around on a beach or a rocky shore. In the water it pushes forward with long front flippers. Look for the small flaps behind the eyes. These are its outer ears, which a true seal lacks. California sea lions also make loud barking calls when many of them gather together.
facts: California sea lions live along the western coast of North America.
An adult male is generally much larger than an adult female.

entries.title: How does a two-toed sloth live upside down?
entries.answer: A two-toed sloth can spend hours hanging from branches in a tropical forest. Its long, curved claws hook over a branch like handles, and strong limbs help hold it in place. It moves slowly through the leaves to feed and rest. Moving slowly and using little energy help on a diet made mostly of plants. A two-toed sloth has two long claws on each front foot, but three on each of its back feet.
facts: A two-toed sloth can swim.
The outer coat can look greenish when algae grow on the hair.

entries.title: How does an Asian elephant use its trunk?
entries.answer: An Asian elephant can pull a branch close, pick up a tiny object, and raise a load of water with the same tool: its trunk. A trunk is an extended nose and upper lip. It bends and twists because it is made of muscle instead of bone. The elephant can suck up water and then pour it into its mouth. It also smells with its trunk and reaches out with it to touch other elephants.
facts: Some male Asian elephants have long tusks. Female Asian elephants usually have much smaller ones or none.
Elephants spend many hours each day feeding on plants.

entries.title: How does an orangutan move in a forest?
entries.answer: Orangutans spend much of their lives above the ground in the forests of Borneo and Sumatra. Their long arms help them reach for branches, and their hands and feet can hold on from different angles. An orangutan may bend a branch toward itself to make the next tree easier to reach. Fruit is an important food. At night, an orangutan can fold leaves and branches together to make a nest that supports its weight well above the ground.
facts: Orangutans are great apes.
A mother orangutan cares for her young for years.

entries.title: How lions live and hunt together
entries.answer: Lions often spend time in groups called prides. Females in a pride are often related, and they may care for cubs together. When several lions hunt, each may take a different position around the animals they are approaching. Living in a group also helps lions defend an area that has food and places to rest. Other big cats live differently. A tiger usually looks for food by itself and does not spend its whole life in a group like a pride.
facts: Most wild lions live in Africa, and some live in India.
Adult male lions often grow a mane around the head and neck.

entries.title: Life underground for naked mole-rats
entries.answer: A naked mole-rat lives in a network of tunnels beneath dry ground in eastern Africa. Its large front teeth stick out in front of its lips, so the animal can chew into dirt without filling its mouth with soil. Groups of mole-rats work in a colony. They extend tunnels, gather roots, or guard the openings. A breeding female and a small number of males have the colony’s young. The other animals do much of the digging and food carrying.
facts: Naked mole-rats are rodents.
Their nearly bare skin has a few hairs that help them feel around.

entries.title: What gives the emperor tamarin its mustached look?
entries.answer: A bearded emperor tamarin is a small monkey with long white whiskers that curve away from its face. Groups move through trees in parts of the western Amazon, eating things like ripe fruit and insects. Its long tail helps balance it during quick movements through branches. Adult males and other group members can help care for young monkeys. A tiny tamarin can ride on an adult’s back before it grows large enough to move easily with the group.
facts: Emperor tamarins are monkeys, rather than apes.
The whiskers gave this monkey its well-known mustached appearance.

entries.title: What helps a tiger hide?
entries.answer: A tiger’s orange and black coat can be hard to make out in tall grass or in a forest with patches of sunlight and shade. Dark stripes break up the shape of its body. This helps a tiger get close to other animals before they notice it. Tigers usually hunt alone and can swim well. They live in several very different parts of Asia, from cold forests in the north to warm islands in the south.
facts: Tigers have their own stripe patterns, so researchers can tell individuals apart in photos.
Tigers can swim across rivers.

entries.title: What makes a cheetah such a fast runner?
entries.answer: A cheetah is built to run fast for a short stretch. Its legs are long and its back can bend and straighten as it runs. Each time its back stretches out, its feet cover more ground. Its claws grip the dirt, and its long tail helps it balance when its path changes quickly. A cheetah usually tries to get fairly close before starting a chase, because its speed only gives it an advantage for a brief time.
facts: Dark marks run from a cheetah’s eyes toward its mouth.
Cheetahs sprint across open ground after animals such as gazelles.

entries.title: What makes an ecosystem
entries.answer: An ecosystem includes living things in a place, the parts of the place that are not alive, and the ways they affect one another. Think of a pond. Sunlight reaches plants and algae in the water. Tiny animals feed on algae, and bigger animals may eat those tiny animals. Bacteria and fungi can break down dead material, making some parts of it available for life to use again. The amount of light, warmth, and water can change which living things do well there. A reef, forest, or puddle can each be an ecosystem.
facts: A food web shows more than one path through which living things get food.
Light and water are parts of an ecosystem even though they are not alive.

entries.title: Why do giant pandas eat so much bamboo?
entries.answer: A giant panda spends much of its day finding and chewing bamboo. Its heavy jaws break tough stems, and a special wrist bone sticks out where a thumb might be. The panda can press a piece of bamboo against its fingers with that bone. Bamboo gives a panda less nourishment than many richer foods would, so the animal eats a great deal of it. In the mountains of central China, pandas move between places where different kinds of bamboo grow.
facts: A panda’s thumb-like grip uses a wrist bone.
Giant pandas belong to the bear family.

entries.title: Why does a meerkat stand on watch?
entries.answer: Meerkats search for insects and other small animals in open, dry parts of southern Africa. When members of the group dig or look closely at the ground, one may climb onto a high spot and watch for danger. A call can warn the others to run to shelter. Meerkats also dig and use underground tunnels. Their burrows offer a safer place to rest and a retreat from the hot ground during part of the day.
facts: Meerkats belong to the mongoose family.
Strong front claws help meerkats dig.

entries.title: Why is the golden frog bright yellow?
entries.answer: The Panamanian golden frog is a small toad with bright yellow skin that often has dark marks. The bright color can warn other animals that the skin contains chemicals they should avoid. Golden frogs live near streams. Where water makes calls hard to hear, a frog can lift and wave a front foot to send a signal to another frog. A deadly fungus has made these frogs extremely rare in the wild, so carefully managed colonies help protect them.
facts: A golden frog is a type of toad.
Golden frogs can communicate by waving one front foot.
